history.summary: Hindu temple at Madhur, ~7 km from Kasaragod town on the banks of the Mogral River (Madhuvahini), where the Kumble 'seme' lore of the region is strong. Shiva as Madanantheshwara (destroyer of Kama, god of desire) is the presiding deity, but Ganapathi as Siddhi Vinayaka facing south in the main sanctum draws the greater devotion. Tradition says the temple was founded when Madaru, an elderly woman of the Tulu Moger community, discovered a self-manifested (udbhava) Shiva linga; a boy's sketch of Ganapathi on the sanctum wall is said to have grown into the idol, called 'Boddajja' (bodda = big/fat). Legend says Tipu Sultan, about to destroy the temple during his invasion, changed his mind after drinking its well water, but left a sword mark on the well's building, still visible. The shrine has a three-tiered gajaprishta (elephant-back) roof and fine wooden carvings from the Ramayana; priests are of the Shivalli Brahmin community. Famous offerings include Appa, Moodappam Seva and Sahasrappa.

name: Madhur Sri Madanantheshwara Vinayaka Temple
town_description: Madhur is a village about 7 km from Kasaragod town in northern Kerala, on the banks of the Mogral River, locally called Madhuvahini. It lies in the Karnataka-Kerala border belt of Kasaragod district where Malayalam, Tulu and Kannada cultures meet. The village is known chiefly for its ancient temple, one of the most visited pilgrimage sites in North Kerala.

travel.road: 7 km from Kasaragod town; frequent private buses and autos from Kasaragod bus stands

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; avoid the monsoon (the Mogral River adjoining the temple can overflow onto the premises)
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM-1:00 PM and 5:30 PM-8:15 PM daily (per the temple's own site, madhurtemple.in; closed 1:00-5:30 PM)
